title: Causal Inference & Causal ML
tagline: Go from 'X is correlated with Y' to 'X causes Y': potential outcomes, causal graphs, matching, natural experiments, and machine learning for treatment effects.
prereqs: Machine Learning. Comfort with regression and basic probability from Python & Math for AI.

steps.title: Causal inference in 15 minutes
steps.why: Why correlation misleads and what causal questions look like.

steps.title: A brief introduction to causal inference
steps.why: Brady Neal's course overview: confounding, interventions, and the big picture.

steps.title: Potential outcomes
steps.why: The Rubin model: compare what happened with what would have happened.

steps.title: Causal graphs
steps.why: Draw assumptions as arrows between variables.

steps.title: Forks, chains, and colliders
steps.why: The three graph patterns that decide what to control for.

steps.title: Causal effects from graphs
steps.why: Backdoor and front-door criteria for handling unobserved confounders.

steps.title: Propensity score matching
steps.why: Compare treated and untreated units that were equally likely to be treated.

steps.title: Instrumental variables
steps.why: Use a variable that shifts treatment but not the outcome directly.

steps.title: Difference-in-differences
steps.why: Compare changes over time between a treated and a control group.

steps.title: Causal inference in Python
steps.why: A conference talk on framing and estimating cause and effect with Python libraries.

steps.title: Machine learning for treatment effects
steps.why: Estimate who benefits most from a treatment with EconML and CausalML.

steps.title: Double machine learning
steps.why: Adjust for many observed confounders with ML; still assumes none are unmeasured.

steps.title: Causal discovery
steps.why: Infer a plausible causal graph from observational data, with a Python example.

projects: Draw a causal graph for a question you care about, list which variables to adjust for, and defend each choice in a short README.
Estimate the effect of job training on earnings with propensity score matching and compare it with a naive difference in means.
Use EconML on a public marketing or uplift dataset to find which customer groups respond most to a treatment.
